proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a same-closure candidate \(G'\) and first work over the rational-function field \(\mathbb K\) generated by the nonzero baseline edge coefficients and intervention-change coefficients.  Acyclicity gives
\[
 P=(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}=I_q+\Lambda^{(0)}+\cdots+(\Lambda^{(0)})^{q-1}.
\]
Consequently, for \(c,k\in V\),
\[
 H_{kc}=h_{kc}=
 \sum_{i\in\operatorname{pa}_{G}(k)}\delta_{ki}P_{ic}.
\]
The right-hand side is exactly the sum of the weights of the directed paths from the original vertex \(c\) to the terminal copy \(k^\star\) in \(G^{\mathrm{term}}\): the last edge of such a path is the uniquely labelled edge \(i\to k^\star\), and the part before it is a baseline path from \(c\) to \(i\).

Let \(C_0\subseteq C\), \(R_0\subseteq R\), and \(|C_0|=|R_0|=m\).  Expanding \(\det H[R_0,C_0]\), and then expanding each matrix entry as a path sum, expresses this determinant as a signed sum over \(m\)-tuples of paths from \(C_0\) to \(R_0^\star\).  If two paths first meet at an original vertex, exchanging their tails after their first common vertex preserves the edge monomial and reverses the endpoint permutation.  It is therefore a sign-reversing involution on intersecting path families.  The uncancelled terms are the vertex-disjoint families.  Moreover, the union of a vertex-disjoint family determines its paths and endpoint permutation, because every internal vertex in that union has one entering and one leaving selected edge.  Thus two surviving families cannot contribute the same edge monomial with opposite signs.  It follows that
\[
 \det H[R_0,C_0]\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{there are \(m\) vertex-disjoint paths from \(C_0\) to \(R_0^\star\)}.
\]
Taking the largest nonzero minor proves
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb K}H[R,C]
 =\max\{m:\text{there are \(m\) vertex-disjoint paths from \(C\) to \(R^\star\)}\}.
\]
The terminal exceptional-polynomial list contains a nonzero maximal path minor whenever the right-hand side is positive.  Hence the same equality holds after specialization at every point of \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,q}(G,G')\).  Vertex splitting, with capacity one on each original vertex, turns the displayed maximum into an ordinary integral maximum-flow computation.

It remains to identify the affine conditions.  Write \(U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\), and for \(i\in C_j\) put \(x_{ji}=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{ij}\).  Direct matrix multiplication gives, for every \(k,j\in V\),
\[
 (HU)_{kj}=H_{kj}-\sum_{i\in C_j}H_{ki}x_{ji}.
\]
Because \(G\) and \(G'\) have the same transitive closure, this entry vanishes automatically when \(k=j\) or \(k\notin\operatorname{de}_{G'}(j)\): in the latter case neither \(j\) nor any child of \(j\) can be an ancestor of \(k\).  For the remaining nonchildren \(k\in R_j\), the required zero is precisely
\[
 H[R_j,C_j]x_j=H[R_j,j],
 \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad M_jx_j=b_j.
\]
For a child \(i\in C_j\), the baseline coefficient, intervention change, and post-change coefficient are respectively
\[
 x_{ji},\qquad
 (HU)_{ij}=H[i,j]-H[i,C_j]x_j=d_{ji}(x_j),
 \qquad x_{ji}+d_{ji}(x_j).
\]
Thus exact baseline support, exact change support, and edge retention are exactly the three asserted nonvanishing requirements.

The linear system is solvable if and only if
\[
 \operatorname{rank}M_j=\operatorname{rank}(M_j\mid b_j).
\]
If it is solvable, write \(\mathcal A_j=x_j^0+\ker M_j\).  An affine form vanishes identically on \(\mathcal A_j\) if and only if it vanishes at \(x_j^0\) and its linear part annihilates \(\ker M_j\); these are row-space conditions on \((M_j\mid b_j)\).  If none of the finitely many forbidden forms vanishes identically, each cuts out a proper affine hyperplane in \(\mathcal A_j\).  A finite union of proper affine hyperplanes cannot cover an affine space over the infinite field \(\mathbb K\).  For example, after choosing affine coordinates \(y\), substitute \(y=(s,s^2,\ldots)\); every nonzero affine form becomes a nonzero univariate polynomial, and one may choose \(s\in\mathbb Q\) outside their finite root set.  Hence one can choose every column \(x_j\) so that all three support conditions hold.  The column blocks are independent, so these choices assemble into a single unit lower-triangular \(U\).  Conversely, every admissible \(U\) supplies a point in each \(\mathcal A_j\) avoiding all forbidden forms.  This proves the claimed equivalence with \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\).  The augmented minors placed in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{term}}\) ensure that consistency and identical-vanishing decisions agree with their rational-function-field decisions throughout the stated generic locus.

There are \(q\) systems of order at most \(q\) and at most \(3|E(G')|\le 3q^2\) row-space tests.  Gaussian elimination separately for all tests uses at most \(O(q^5)\) operations in \(\mathbb K\); this is a field-operation bound and does not claim polynomial expanded bit complexity.  A failed rank equality or a row-space identity is a nonmembership certificate, while a rational point avoiding the forbidden forms is a membership certificate.

Finally, there are finitely many labelled DAGs on \(V\).  Enumerating those with closure \(\overline G\), applying the preceding tests, and comparing their truth values with the baseline inverse-path rank tests defining \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G)\) proves the exact agreement characterization and gives a terminating graph-input procedure.  The possible disagreement is real: for \(G_\times\), \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\), and \(j=1\), direct path expansion gives the actual-row augmented determinant
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}\beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\
 \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix}=\gamma(\beta d-b\delta),
\]
which is not the zero polynomial, whereas the baseline-path rows are proportional.  The terminal argument nowhere uses \(v\) or \(t\), so it remains valid when \(t_k=v_k\).

The two graphs have the same transitive closure, namely the total reachability order \(1<2<3<4\).  For \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\) and \(j=1\), one has \(C_1=\{2\}\) and \(R_1=\{3,4\}\).  In \(G_\times\), path expansion of \(P=(I_4-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) gives
\[
 P[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 b&d+\alpha b\\
 cb&c(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its second row is \(c\) times its first row.  Since \(b\ne0\), both \(P[\{3,4\},\{2\}]\) and the displayed augmented matrix have rank one.  The other baseline tests also pass: for \(j=2\), \(C_2=\{3\}\), \(R_2=\{4\}\), and the row \((P_{43},P_{42})=(c,cb)\) has the same rank as its first entry; for \(j=3,4\), the relevant nonchild-descendant sets are empty.  Therefore \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{obs}}(G_\times)\).

The actual intervention rows are obtained from \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}P\).  At targets three and four this gives
\[
 h_3^{\mathsf T}=(\delta+\alpha\beta,\beta,0,0),
 \qquad
 h_4^{\mathsf T}=(\gamma(d+\alpha b),\gamma b,\gamma,0).
\]
Hence
\[
 H[\{3,4\},\{2\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}\beta\\ \gamma b\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 \beta&\delta+\alpha\beta\\
 \gamma b&\gamma(d+\alpha b)
 \end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
 \det H[\{3,4\},\{2,1\}]
 =\gamma\{\beta(d+\alpha b)-b(\delta+\alpha\beta)\}
 =\gamma(\beta d-b\delta).
\]
This polynomial is nonzero: at \(\alpha=b=c=d=\beta=\gamma=1\) and \(\delta=2\) it equals \(-1\).  Taking also \(\delta_{21}=1\), the post-change edge coefficients are \(2\) on \(1\to2\), \(2\) on \(2\to3\), \(3\) on \(1\to3\), and \(2\) on \(3\to4\).  Thus every baseline edge, every required change, and every retained edge is nonzero.  The nonvanishing determinant persists on a nonempty relative Zariski-open subset, which meets \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{term},p,4}(G_\times,G_{\mathrm{ch}})\).  On that subset the unaugmented rank is one and the augmented rank is two, so the affine system for column one is inconsistent.  The terminal-certificate theorem therefore gives \(G_{\mathrm{ch}}\notin\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_\times)\).

If one makes the specialization \((\beta,\delta)=(b,d)\), the same determinant becomes \(\gamma(bd-bd)=0\).  Since \((\beta,\delta)\) are intervention-change coordinates while \((b,d)\) are baseline-edge coordinates, exact support and retention impose only nonvanishing conditions and do not justify these two equalities.  The specialization therefore lies on a proper algebraic subset and can reduce generic rank.  No variance entered the calculation, so the mismatch holds throughout the positive-variance ambient domain.

Put \(B=I_q-\Lambda^{(0)}\).  Since \(G\) is acyclic and \(\delta_k\) is supported on parents of \(k\),
\[
 h_{kk}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}Pe_k=0.
\]
Multiplication, rather than an unverified division, now proves the inverse formula:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (B-e_k\delta_k^{\mathsf T})(P+Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T})
 &=I_q+e_kh_k^{\mathsf T}-e_k\delta_k^{\mathsf T}P
   -e_k(\delta_k^{\mathsf T}Pe_k)h_k^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=I_q.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
 (I_q-\Lambda^{(k)})^{-1}=P+Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T},
 \quad
 \Delta^{(k)}=Pe_kh_k^{\mathsf T},
 \quad
 \Delta^{(k)}_{k,\cdot}=h_k^{\mathsf T},
 \quad
 A^{(k)}=A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T},
\]
where the third identity uses \(P_{kk}=1\).  Also \(A^{(k)}e_k=a_k\).  Expanding the covariance and using \(S^{(k)}=S+(t_k-v_k)e_ke_k^{\mathsf T}\) therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_k
 &=(A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T})S(A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}-ASA^{\mathsf T}
 +(t_k-v_k)a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}\\
 &=a_k(ASh_k)^{\mathsf T}+(ASh_k)a_k^{\mathsf T}
 +(h_k^{\mathsf T}Sh_k+t_k-v_k)a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently, with
\[
 w_k=ASh_k+\frac{h_k^{\mathsf T}Sh_k+t_k-v_k}{2}a_k,
\]
one has \(D_k=a_kw_k^{\mathsf T}+w_ka_k^{\mathsf T}\).

On the branch-generic locus, a root has \(h_k=0\) and \(t_k-v_k\ne0\), so \(D_k=(t_k-v_k)a_ka_k^{\mathsf T}\) has one factor line.  At a nonroot the exceptional discriminants exclude proportionality of \(a_k\) and \(w_k\); hence \(D_k\) has rank two and is indefinite.  To see that there are exactly two factor lines, suppose
\[
 a_kw_k^{\mathsf T}+w_ka_k^{\mathsf T}
 =\ell m^{\mathsf T}+m\ell^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For every indeterminate vector \(y\), equality of quadratic forms gives
\[
 (y^{\mathsf T}a_k)(y^{\mathsf T}w_k)
 =(y^{\mathsf T}\ell)(y^{\mathsf T}m).
\]
The ranges on both sides show that \(\ell,m\in\operatorname{span}(a_k,w_k)\).  In the ordered basis \((a_k,w_k)\), write \(\ell=(r,s)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(m=(u,v)^{\mathsf T}\).  Comparing the two diagonal coefficients and the cross coefficient gives
\[
 ru=0,\qquad sv=0,\qquad rv+su\ne0.
\]
The last inequality also says that \(\ell,m\) are independent.  Hence either \(r=v=0\) or \(s=u=0\), so the unordered pair of lines \(\{\mathbb Ra_k,\mathbb Rw_k\}\) equals \(\{\mathbb R\ell,\mathbb Rm\}\).  Thus each nonroot supplies two choices and each root one, for at most \(2^{q-r}\) choices per common-permutation representative.

Fix one such choice and use the allowed nonzero diagonal source scaling to set the candidate baseline reduced mixing equal to \(L=[\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q]\).  Equality of baseline covariances is exactly
\[
 L\operatorname{diag}(v')L^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma^{(0)}.
\]
For a genuine candidate define
\[
 z_k=\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_k,
 \qquad
 \rho_k=\frac{h_k'{}^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(v')h'_k+t'_k-v'_k}{2}.
\]
The covariance-difference identity already proved then gives
\[
 m_k=Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k,
 \qquad
 t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\sum_{i=1}^q\frac{z_{ki}^2}{v'_i}.
\]
Because \(h'_k=\delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}U^{-1}\), it is supported on \(\operatorname{an}_{G'}(k)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}=h'_k{}^{\mathsf T}U
 =z_k^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(v')^{-1}U.
\]
This proves that every legal twin enters one of the displayed systems, including a twin with \(t'_k=v'_k\).

Conversely, suppose a branch system is feasible.  Positivity of every \(v'_i\) makes \(h'_k=\operatorname{diag}(v')^{-1}z_k\) well defined, and the asserted formula for \(t'_k\) makes its positivity inequality exactly the required candidate intervention-variance condition.  Set
\[
 \Lambda'^{(0)}=I_q-U,
 \qquad F'=LU,
 \qquad \delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}=h'_k{}^{\mathsf T}U.
\]
The support and retained-edge inequations make this a member of \(\mathcal M_{p,q}(G')\).  The baseline moment equation and \(v'>0\) imply \(\operatorname{rank}L=p\), since \(\Sigma^{(0)}\) is positive definite; hence \(F'=LU\) has full row rank.  The remaining branch inequations give nonzero, pairwise-noncollinear columns of \(F'\).  Applying the covariance identity to the candidate and substituting \(m_k=Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k\) reproduces every \(D_k\), and the baseline equation reproduces \(\Sigma^{(0)}\).  Thus no illegal solution is admitted and no legal twin is lost.

All divisions used above are guarded by \(v'_i>0\) or by a chart-denominator inequation.  The finite common-permutation enumeration and rational projective gauges exhaust the permutation, sign, and scale indeterminacies.  Every polynomial retained in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{branch}}\) is nonzero as a polynomial after graph-specific identically zero factors are removed.  A nonzero real polynomial cannot vanish on a relatively open chamber: restricting it successively to coordinate lines in an open box would otherwise make all its coefficients zero.  Hence its zero set has empty relative interior in every full-dimensional ambient chamber.  In particular, \(\prod_k(t_k-v_k)\) removes only the source-null and variance-neutral true hyperplanes, while the two signs of each variance change lie in adjacent covered chambers; no candidate variance-neutral hyperplane is removed.

Let \(U=I_4-\Lambda^{(0)}\) and \(U'=I_4-\Lambda'^{(0)}\) for the two points in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{fork}}(T)\).  From the displayed construction,
\[
 F=AU=\begin{pmatrix}-8&-9&7&4\\-12&-15&11&7\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 F'=AU'=\begin{pmatrix}-7&-9&7&4\\-10&-15&11&7\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus both baseline reduced mixing matrices are exactly \(A\).  The six pairwise column determinants of \(F\) are
\[
 12,-4,-8,6,-3,5,
\]
and those of \(F'\) are
\[
 15,-7,-9,6,-3,5.
\]
They are all nonzero, proving full row rank, nonzero columns, and pairwise noncollinearity.

Multiplication of the actual rows by the two structural factors gives
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cccc}
 k&1&2&3&4\\ \hline
 \delta_k^{\mathsf T}&0&(1,0,0,0)&(2,1,0,0)&(0,1,0,0)\\
 \delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}&0&(1,0,0,0)&(0,8/11,0,0)&(0,-1/2,0,0).
 \end{array}
\]
These rows have exactly the parent supports of \(G_{\mathrm{fork}}\) and \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\).  Adding them to the corresponding baseline rows gives nonzero post-change coefficients: in the true model they are \(2\), \((3,2)\), and \(2\), and in the candidate they are \(5\), \(19/11\), and \(1/2\), for targets two, three, and four respectively.

Using the covariance identity from \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\), or multiplying the displayed rational matrices directly, both models give the following five matrices:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Sigma^{(0)}&=\begin{pmatrix}70&113\\113&183\end{pmatrix},&
 \Sigma^{(1)}&=\begin{pmatrix}73&119\\119&195\end{pmatrix},\\
 \Sigma^{(2)}&=\begin{pmatrix}90&144\\144&231\end{pmatrix},&
 \Sigma^{(3)}&=\begin{pmatrix}49T+581&77T+924\\77T+924&121T+1470\end{pmatrix},\\
 \Sigma^{(4)}&=\begin{pmatrix}174&294\\294&498\end{pmatrix}.&&
 \end{aligned}
\]
Their determinants are, in the same order,
\[
 41,\quad 74,\quad 54,\quad 7(5T+42),\quad 216.
\]
Their leading entries are positive for \(T>0\), so all five are positive definite.  The candidate variances are positive because
\[
 T+\frac{144}{121}>0,
 \qquad \frac{19}{4}>0.
\]
Relative to the unit baseline variances, the true variance changes are \(3,3,T-1,3\), all nonzero when \(T\ne1\), and the candidate changes are \(3,3,T+23/121,15/4\), all nonzero when \(T>0\).

For existence of the required error laws, in each context take mutually independent Rademacher variables \(R_i^{(k)}\) and put \(\varepsilon_i^{(k)}=\sqrt{S^{(k)}_{ii}}R_i^{(k)}\), with the primed analogue for the candidate.  These coordinates are centered, independent, non-Gaussian, and have exactly the displayed positive diagonal covariance matrices.

Finally, for the candidate deletion of \(1\to3\), the column-one affine consistency determinant formed from the true actual rows is
\[
 \det\begin{pmatrix}H_{32}&H_{31}\\H_{42}&H_{41}\end{pmatrix}
 =\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=-2.
\]
The terminal-certificate theorem therefore excludes \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\) from \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\).  All assertions are exact rational identities; no algebraic-independence assumption is used.  The finite exceptional-polynomial definition, rather than the existence of this one-dimensional family, separately determines whether a particular displayed point belongs to a theorem-specific generic locus.

On the fork generic locus, node one is the only root and nodes two, three, and four have rank-two covariance differences.  The factor-line argument in \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\) therefore gives one choice for node one and two choices for each of the other three nodes, hence exactly \(1\cdot2^3=8\) regular line branches.

These regularity polynomials are genuinely nonzero for every one of the eight choices.  Indeed, at the true point \(T=2\), the unnormalized factor choices are
\[
 \ell_1=(1,2)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 \ell_2\in\{(2,3)^{\mathsf T},(5,8)^{\mathsf T}\},\quad
 \ell_3\in\{(7,11)^{\mathsf T},(87/2,139/2)^{\mathsf T}\},
\]
and
\[
 \ell_4\in\{(4,7)^{\mathsf T},(13,45/2)^{\mathsf T}\}.
\]
For the four choices of \((\ell_2,\ell_3)\), the determinant of the first three columns of \(B_\ell\) is respectively
\[
 3,\qquad \frac{595}{4},\qquad -6,\qquad -\frac{35}{2},
\]
independently of the choice of \(\ell_4\).  Moreover,
\[
 \det[\ell_1,\ell_2]\in\{-1,-2\},
 \qquad
 \det[\ell_3,\ell_4]\in\left\{5,\frac{29}{2},\frac{53}{2},\frac{301}{4}\right\}.
\]
All these numbers are nonzero.  Hence the corresponding minors are nonzero polynomials, and their inclusion in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\) makes all eight branches regular on the stated generic locus.

Fix a branch and its projectively normalized columns \(\ell_k\).  Since \(p=2\), the baseline covariance equation is equivalent entry by entry to
\[
 B_{\ell}v'=\operatorname{vech}(\Sigma^{(0)}),
 \qquad
 B_{\ell}=\bigl[(\ell_{k1}^2,\ell_{k1}\ell_{k2},\ell_{k2}^2)^{\mathsf T}\bigr]_{k=1}^4.
\]
The fork exceptional locus removes the failure of every selected nonzero \(3\times3\) minor, so \(\operatorname{rank}B_{\ell}=3\).  Its solution set is consequently either empty or the affine line
\[
 v'=v'_0+sn,
 \qquad n\in\ker B_{\ell}\setminus\{0\}.
\]
Feasibility further requires the four explicit inequalities \(v'_i>0\).

The selected determinant conditions make \(\ell_1,\ell_2\) a basis of \(\mathbb R^2\), so there are unique \(\zeta,\rho_2\) such that
\[
 m_2=\zeta\ell_1+\rho_2\ell_2.
\]
For \(G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\), exact support at node two gives \(z_2=(\zeta,0,0,0)\), and the general branch equations therefore yield
\[
 h'_2=(\zeta/v'_1,0,0,0),
 \qquad
 t'_2=v'_2+2\rho_2-\frac{\zeta^2}{v'_1}.
\]
The divisions are valid because \(v'_1>0\), and exact change support requires \(\zeta\ne0\).

Put \(x=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{21}\).  For \(k=3,4\), the candidate has the sole parent \(2\), while its ancestors are \(1,2\).  If \(h'_k=(r_1,r_2,0,0)\), then multiplication by \(U=I_4-\Lambda'^{(0)}\) gives
\[
 \delta'_{k1}=r_1-xr_2,
 \qquad \delta'_{k2}=r_2.
\]
Exact support is therefore equivalent to \(h'_k=\beta_k(x,1,0,0)\) with \(\beta_k\ne0\).  It follows that
\[
 z_k=(v'_1\beta_kx,v'_2\beta_k,0,0),
 \qquad Lz_k=\beta_k g,
 \qquad g=v'_1x\ell_1+v'_2\ell_2.
\]
The factor equation \(m_k=Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k\) becomes
\[
 m_k-\beta_kg=\rho_k\ell_k.
\]
Taking determinants with \(\ell_k\) proves
\[
 \beta_k=\frac{\det[m_k,\ell_k]}{\det[g,\ell_k]}.
\]
The numerator is nonzero because \(D_k\) has rank two.  Thus a vanishing denominator cannot be part of a feasible branch and is correctly excluded.  Substitution into the Schur-complement variance formula gives
\[
 t'_k=v'_k+2\rho_k-\beta_k^2(v'_1x^2+v'_2),
\]
with the strict inequality \(t'_k>0\).  No step divides by \(t'_k-v'_k\), so candidate variance neutrality is allowed.

It remains to reconstruct the candidate structural mixing.  Write \(b=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{32}\) and \(c=\Lambda'^{(0)}_{42}\).  Then
\[
 F'=LU
 =\bigl[\ell_1-x\ell_2,\ \ell_2-b\ell_3-c\ell_4,\ \ell_3,\ \ell_4\bigr].
\]
The branch inequations already require the first, third, and fourth displayed columns to be nonzero and pairwise noncollinear.  Since \(\det[\ell_3,\ell_4]\ne0\), the affine map
\[
 (b,c)\longmapsto \ell_2-b\ell_3-c\ell_4
\]
is onto \(\mathbb R^2\).  Nonzeroness and noncollinearity of its image, the conditions \(b,c\ne0\), and retention \(b+\beta_3\ne0\), \(c+\beta_4\ne0\), exclude only finitely many proper affine lines in the \((b,c)\)-plane.  Their complement is nonempty, so such \(b,c\) exist.

The necessity of every equation follows from the complete covariance-branch lemma.  Conversely, from a solution choose \(b,c\) as above, set \(F'=LU\), set \(\delta'_k=h'_k{}^{\mathsf T}U\), and use the displayed positive variances.  The baseline moment equation gives \(\Sigma'^{(0)}=\Sigma^{(0)}\); for each target the equality \(m_k=Lz_k+\rho_k\ell_k\) and the variance formula reproduce \(D_k\) by the already-proved covariance identity.  Hence all five original covariance equations hold.  This proves soundness and completeness of the regular two-scalar reduction.  Finally, \(\mathrm{prop:fork\text{-}rational\text{-}collision}\) supplies a legal twin for every \(T>0\), \(T\ne1\), so its parameters necessarily solve one of the eight complete branch systems.

Fix \(G'\in\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\), and let \(C\) be a full-dimensional connected sign-and-variance chamber in \(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\).  Intersecting \(C\) with the terminal generic locus removes only finitely many proper polynomial zero sets, so the intersection is relatively dense in \(C\).  At every point of that intersection, the terminal-certificate theorem supplies a unit lower-triangular matrix \(U=I_q-\Lambda'^{(0)}\) with exact support \(G'\) such that
\[
 \delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}=h_k^{\mathsf T}U
\]
has exact candidate parent support and retains every candidate edge.

Define a candidate by
\[
 P'=U^{-1},\qquad A'=A,qquad F'=AU,qquad
 v'=v,qquad t'=t,qquad h'_k=h_k.
\]
Then \(F'P'=A\), and
\[
 \delta'_k{}^{\mathsf T}P'=h_k^{\mathsf T}UU^{-1}=h_k^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The inverse-update identity gives, context by context,
\[
 F'(I_q-\Lambda'^{(k)})^{-1}
 =A'+A'e_kh'_k{}^{\mathsf T}
 =A+a_kh_k^{\mathsf T}
 =A^{(k)}.
\]
Because the candidate uses the same positive diagonal variances, it follows immediately that
\[
 \Sigma'^{(k)}=\Sigma^{(k)}qquad(k\in K).
\]

It remains only to check candidate mixing admissibility.  The columns of the invertible matrix \(U\) are nonzero and no two are collinear.  For any fixed admissible \(U\), the conditions that a column of \(AU\) vanish or that two columns be collinear are polynomial equations in the entries of the full-row-rank matrix \(A\).  None is the zero polynomial: a generic linear map \(\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^p\), with \(p\ge2\), sends a fixed finite set of pairwise noncollinear nonzero vectors to pairwise noncollinear nonzero vectors.  The simultaneous conditions that \(A(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})\) also have admissible columns are likewise complements of proper polynomial zero sets.  On each rational rank chart of the affine terminal solution, choose one rational admissible section \(U\); the preceding bad sets remain proper on that chart.  Hence points for which \(F'=AU\) is legal form a relatively dense subset of \(C\).  Full row rank is automatic because \(A\) has rank \(p\) and \(U\) is invertible.

Thus \(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\cap C\) is relatively dense in \(C\), so
\[
 C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(\mathcal E_p(G,G')\cap C)=\varnothing.
\]
This holds for every full-dimensional chamber, which is precisely \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\).  The construction preserves the sign of every true variance change, uses no division by \(t_k-v_k\), and permits candidate neutrality in the definition even though the particular witness takes \(t'=t\).  The covariance class makes no pointwise assertion on excluded true variance-neutral hyperplanes, exactly as claimed.

For a fixed representative, the inverse-update identity gives
\[
 A^{(k)}-A^{(0)}=a_kh_k^{\mathsf T}.
\]
On the intersection with the branch generic locus, \(a_k\ne0\), so the scalar multiplier of \(a_k\) in each column of this rank-one difference is unique; the constraint \(h_{kk}=0\) therefore recovers the actual row \(h_k\).

For \(i,k\in V\), path expansion gives
\[
 h_{ki}=\sum_{j\in\operatorname{pa}_G(k)}\delta_{kj}P_{ji}.
\]
If \(i\notin\operatorname{an}_G(k)\), every summand is zero.  If \(i\in\operatorname{an}_G(k)\), the right-hand side is the terminal-path polynomial from \(i\) to \(k^\star\); it is not the zero polynomial because at least one such path exists.  The terminal generic locus excludes its vanishing.  Hence
\[
 (H_{\mathcal R})_{ki}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i\in\operatorname{an}_G(k),
\]
which is exactly \(\mathcal C(\mathcal R)=\overline G\).

Now first consider a diagonal representative change \(C=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_q)\).  Since
\[
 A^{(k)}C-A^{(0)}C
 =a_kh_k^{\mathsf T}C
 =(c_ka_k)(c_k^{-1}h_k^{\mathsf T}C),
\]
the recovered row changes to \(c_k^{-1}h_k^{\mathsf T}C\).  Multiplication by nonzero diagonal entries preserves its zero pattern.  A common permutation merely conjugates this relation and relabels all intervention targets.  Thus the recovered closure changes only by the permutation part of the monomial action.

The same calculation shows invariance of every terminal rank and every zero or nonzero support condition.  Latent rescaling sends a candidate variance to a positive squared rescaling of that variance and transports \(F'\), \(\Lambda'\), and \(\delta'\) bijectively, without changing any observed covariance.  Therefore covariance feasibility and any explicit realization witness are invariant.  The inverse transport preserves nonmembership separators as well.  Normalizing each nonzero loading column by its least-index nonzero observed coordinate sets that coordinate to one and uniquely removes the diagonal factor; only the finite common permutation orbit remains.  Since both graph-set definitions quantify over the corresponding transported model points, the two maps and their set difference are independent of the chosen representative.

The final limitation follows from the definitions themselves.  Membership in \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cov}}\) asks for a twin at the one supplied covariance tuple, whereas membership in \(\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\) asks whether the twin set is dense after closure in every full-dimensional chamber.  Density neither states nor implies membership of every point in a dense semialgebraic set.  Likewise, the observable soft class is pointwise in \(\mathcal R\), while \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G)\) is defined by a generic graph-wide quantifier.  No frozen assumption supplies the missing constancy implication, so only the quotient invariance and pointwise functional assertion follow.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct the claimed bagwise elimination and branch-gluing algorithm and prove that its projected cells are relatively dense exactly when \(G'\in\mathsf{Cov}_p(G)\), with the stated bit-operation and certificate-height bounds.
open_obligations.obstruction: The definitions of \(\mathfrak C_p(G,G')\) and \(\omega_p(G,G')\) name terminal states, Schur cells, subresultants, and branch gluing but do not specify transition rules or prove projection completeness.  Positivity of the baseline covariance decomposition couples variables across bags, and eliminating a bag may create resultants involving variables outside the declared active frontier.  No frozen lemma bounds that fill-in, controls recursive covariance-cone faces, or derives the exponents \(2^{w+3}\) and \(2^{w+2}\).  Treating the construction text as those proofs would smuggle the theorem into its definition.
open_obligations.attempted: Applied the exact terminal affine decomposition, the finite factor-line reduction, and the fork two-scalar elimination pattern.  These yield correct local systems, but the step from local sign tables to a chamberwise dense projection requires a uniform gluing invariant that is absent; unrestricted real quantifier elimination would decide the resulting formulas but is explicitly disallowed by the claim.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved terminal algorithm decides every actual-row affine block in \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field operations, and the covariance lemma reduces every regular covariance twin to at most \(2^{q-r}\) explicit positive-real factor-line systems.  For the four-node fork, each such system reduces further to two candidate scalars \((s,x)\).  These results supply the local states a bounded-width compiler would have to combine, but they do not prove that local subresultant tables glue without global fill-in or establish the displayed bit and coefficient bounds.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Give a graph-specific, non-quantifier-elimination criterion deciding density of the projection of the complete union of legal positive-real covariance branches in every full-dimensional true chamber, together with realization or separator certificates and uniform complexity.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite branch representation does not control projection of a union: alternate loading lines, nonunique positive baseline decompositions, support hyperplanes, and Schur-positivity regions can meet after elimination.  A successful rational branch or nonsingular local Jacobian proves only local interior, while failure of one branch is not a separator for their union.  The frozen core contains no invariant proving that these interactions are localized for arbitrary graph pairs, and the supplied draft explicitly records this all-graph projection-completeness step as open.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced general regular twins to \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), derived the fork's eight bivariate systems, and verified the rational collision against the original five covariance equations.  The remaining classification would require eliminating the candidate variables uniformly over all true parameters; the available route is unrestricted real quantifier elimination, which does not satisfy the question's non-QE requirement.
open_obligations.partial_result: Every regular covariance twin is represented by the finite family \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\), so unrestricted real-algebraic projection would decide each fixed graph pair.  The terminal part already has linkage and affine certificates, and the four-node fork has an exact eight-branch reduction to bivariate rational sign systems with an explicit positive collision.  What remains is a uniform non-quantifier-elimination argument proving that the union of all positive branches has dense projection, or producing a full-dimensional separator, in every true sign-and-variance chamber.
